source.title: Open Source Replication of Anthropic’s Crosscoder paper for model-diffing

record.file_problem: Whole post and comments are present; not garbled or cut off.
record.tranche_reason: Applies a sparse crosscoder to Gemma-2 2B base and IT residual streams, extending sparse-dictionary feature analysis to LLMs and reporting sparsity and reconstruction results.
record.gate_note: The post reports crosscoder sparsity and reconstruction metrics relevant to whether a sparse dictionary can recover features in real models. Its cluster counts, decoder-vector alignment findings, and hand-picked latent examples are reported as model-diffing results, but do not directly test the other claim versions. Results cited from Anthropic are not counted as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The post trains a sparse crosscoder (an SAE on concatenated Gemma-2 2B base and IT residual streams) as a model-diffing tool. It reports only that tool's own SAE-style performance (L0, explained variance, CE recovered) and its model-diffing findings. It never asks whether features are superposed, whether neurons are polysemantic, or whether sparse features exist in the model as such. Reconstruction metrics of the study's own dictionary are method-performance numbers, not a test of V4. The few latent examples are hand-picked by the authors, not a measured test. So this is T4, not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say Anthropic's core crosscoder results replicate on Gemma-2 2B: latents form three relative-norm clusters, and shared latents mostly have aligned decoder vectors, with some exceptions. They report an unexplained excess of chat-specific (~225) over base-specific (~60) latents. They judge the crosscoder (L0 81, ~77% explained variance, ~95% CE recovered) a viable interpretability tool with substantial room for improvement.
record.recipe_differences: This is an SAE-style crosscoder trained on the middle-layer residual streams of a base and an IT model, rather than a toy-network study of superposition. The post describes it as a replication of Anthropic's crosscoder results, not a reproduction of Toy Models of Superposition.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors note that the observed imbalance between chat-specific and base-specific latents could reflect the Gemma-2 2B models or training setup; they do not establish which. Hyperparameters were not systematically tuned.

fits_no_version.finding: Crosscoder latents cluster into shared, base-specific (~60) and chat-specific (~225) groups by relative decoder norm. Most shared latents have highly aligned decoder vectors across base and IT models, with some low or negative cosine exceptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning preserves most dictionary features across base and chat models, with a small set of model-specific features.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to one Gemma-2 2B base/IT pair and one mixed training distribution. The evaluation uses 4096 activations and 40 sequences; uncertainty estimates are not reported. The authors say hyperparameters were not systematically tuned and that only a handful of cherry-picked latents were inspected.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant metric rows omitted. Cluster counts, shared-vector cosine findings, and selected latent examples are not separate rows because they do not directly measure the feature-recovery claim in V4.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep, phase transition or geometry.
No test of capacity competition or dedicated dimensions for important features.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.

Uses a sparse dictionary as a tool. It does not test whether features are spread across neurons, or whether the model genuinely contains the recovered sparse features; there are no controls or baselines.
No test of completeness, stability or canonicity of dictionary features.
No comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3/V4 supports' verdict is reclassified. The SAE-style metrics evaluate the authors' own dictionary as a tool and do not test whether superposition or sparse features exist in the model. The latent examples are explicitly cherry-picked from a handful inspected. Hyperparameters were not tuned and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature sparsity sweep, transition, or regular geometry are tested.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
Tests sparse dictionary recovery on one Gemma-2 2B base/IT model pair, but not feature spread across neurons or generalization across models, training distributions, or dictionary methods.
Does not test whether dictionary features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Gemma-2-2b base and Gemma-2-2b-it, on the Pile + Lmsys mix
reader_labels.reason: The crosscoder has L0 81 and reports reconstruction results of 77.90% and 77.56% explained variance and 95.43% and 95.67% CE loss recovered relative to zero ablation (r1–r7). This supports sparse-dictionary recovery in this tested setting.
